1291. 0. T. Rosenberch. — Smi l von Gratzen schenkt dem Stifte die Kirche in Deutsch - Reichenau und nebstdem den dritten Theil der Zehnten von den Deutschreichenauer Pfarrdörfern.

XLI. Diuino atestante eloquio didici, quia quicquid misericorditer ac respectu pietatis inpenditur, et auctorem snum adiuuare et in die remuneracionis optatum ei premium a&portare (sic). Sciant igitur presentes ac posteri, quod ego Zmielo de Graetzen diuinis inspira- cionibus informatus ecclesiam meam in Reychenaw, cuins collacio et ¡us patronatus iure hereditario ad me spectat, tradidi domui beate Marie virginis in Hohenfvrt ordinis Cysterciensis cum tercia parte omnium decimarum cunctarum villarum, que ad prefatam dinoscuntur 46 ecclesiam pertinere, iure perpetuo possidendam in meorum pecca- minum remissionem et ob remedium propinquorum meorum, qui de hoc seculo migrauerunt, sperans per hec et alia beneficia, quibus deum honorare desidero in seruis suis, quandoque aput dominum omnium bonorum retributorem misericordiam inuenire. Hoc etiam uolui memorie commendandum, quod eiusdem ecclesie plebanus no mine Paeblo, cui eandem contuli, propter deum eam- possideat ad dies suos; post mortem uero predicti sacerdotis antedicte ecclesie collacio spectat ad abbatem et conuentum in Hohenfvrt pleno iure. Vt autem bec rata permaneant et nulla queant inposterumcalumpnia perturbari, presentem cartam predictis fratribus tradidi meo sigillo et dilecti cognati mei domini Hainrici deRosenberch sigillimunimine roboratam. Huius rei testes sunt: Dominus Hainricus cogimtus meus de Rosenberch, dominus Hainricus et dominus Wocho fratres dicti de Chrvmbenaw , dominus Albertus de Strobnitz, dominus Beuisius de Horach, dominus Shenko de Dvdlieh, Dwrsata de Cypping, W atz laus purcrauius de Rosenberch, Albero etBvdilaus fratres de Horach, et alii quam plures. Actum anno in Rosenberch anno domini M°CC° nonagesimo primo. 1. Die beiden,an Pergamentstreifen hängenden Siegel sind gut erhalten- a) Ziemlich gross und in weiesem Wachs abgedruckt. — Ein Schild mit der fünfbläürigen Rose. — f S. Zmilonis. De. Gretzen (oder Gretzen?). b) Das zweite Siegel ist klein und in grünes Wachs gedruckt. — Spuren eines Schildes, dessen Zeichen aber nicht mehr erkennbar ist, mit einem Helm darüber, dessen Schmuck in dem Brustbilde eines schwertschwingenden Mannes besteht. — Sigil- Wilhelmi. De Roscnberk. Millauer hat dieses Siegel nicht genau untersucht und daher übersehen, dass dasselbeschonnach seiner äusseren Gestalt einer anderen Zeit angehören müsse. Vergl. seinen Ursprung p. 107, Anm. 162. Ich unterlasse es, darüber, wie das Siegel einer bedeutend späteren Zeit und eines später lebenden Mannes an diese Urkunde gehängt werden konnte, Vermuthungen auszusprechen. 2. Millauer p. 105, n. 23. — Trajer a. a. 0. p. 290.
entries.english: I, Smil von Gratzen, moved by divine inspiration, have given my church at Deutsch-Reichenau to the house of Saint Mary the Virgin at Hohenfurt, of the Cistercian order, together with one third of all the tithes from every village known to belong to that church, to be held in perpetuity. The right of presentation and patronage of the church belongs to me by hereditary right. I make this gift for the remission of my sins and for the benefit of my relatives who have departed this life, hoping thereby to find mercy with the Lord, the giver of all good things. I also stipulate that the parish priest of that church, named Paeblo, to whom I have granted it, may possess it for his lifetime for God’s sake; after his death, the right of presentation to the church shall belong fully to the abbot and convent at Hohenfurt. To keep the grant firm and free from future challenge, I give this charter to the brothers, confirmed with my seal and that of my beloved kinsman Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg. Witnesses: Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg, my kinsman; Lords Heinrich and Wok, brothers called von Krumau; Lord Albert von Strobnitz; Lord Benisius von Horach; Lord Shenko von Doudleby; Dwrsata von Cipping; Watzlaus, Burggraf zu Rosenberg; the brothers Albero and Budilaus von Horach; and many others. Enacted at Rosenberg in 1291. The two seals hang from parchment strips and are well preserved. The first is rather large, impressed in white wax, and shows a shield with a five-leaved rose; its inscription reads “Seal of Smil von Gratzen.” The second is small, impressed in green wax, and shows traces of a shield whose device is no longer recognizable, with a helmet above it bearing the bust of a man swinging a sword; its inscription reads “Seal of Wilhelm von Rosenberg.” Millauer did not examine this seal closely and therefore overlooked that its outward form must belong to a different period. Compare his Origin, p. 107, note 162. I refrain from speculating how a seal from a significantly later period, belonging to a man who lived later, came to be attached to this charter. Reference: Millauer, p. 105, no. 23; Trajer, same work, p. 290.
